Why the best bread takes three days
And why your sourdough keeps going flat.

Most bread recipes are written for speed. Ninety minutes, maybe two hours, and you have a loaf. But almost every baker who's obsessed with flavour will tell you the same thing: time is the most important ingredient.
When dough rests slowly in a cold fridge, yeast and bacteria have time to break starches down into sugars and acids. That's where the deep, slightly sour, almost nutty taste comes from.
Here's the three-day schedule I use every week, with the exact temperatures and timings.

Day one: mix the starter at 8pm and leave it at room temperature overnight. Day two: mix the dough in the morning, fold it four times, then shape and refrigerate. Day three: bake straight from the fridge in a very hot pot.
The single biggest mistake? Under-proofing. If your loaf is dense with big holes at the top, give it another hour.
